rules.rule: Engine core: producer thread, ring buffer, and the audio callback path. The callback is real-time: flag any heap allocation (Vec/String/Box/format!/to_owned/collect), any mutex or RwLock acquisition, any blocking I/O, any unbounded loop, and any panic path (unwrap/expect/panic!/indexing) that can be reached from the render or process loop. Buffers must be preallocated before the stream starts. On ring-buffer underrun, write silence rather than stalling. Producer must stay paced by the device callback count. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

Pure DSP, no I/O. Flag any file or network I/O, any allocation inside the process/deck render path, and any state that is mutated without a clear per-block boundary. Channel mapping is stereo: a bus maps to a stereo pair or a single mono channel (1-based), with mono folding L+R * 0.5. Sample-rate and buffer-size handling must stay consistent with engine-core (48 kHz / 512-frame defaults). Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

flutter_rust_bridge host layer. UI widgets must never call raw host invoke/listen; all engine and library I/O goes through the transport types (EngineTransport, LibraryTransport, ControllerTransport). engine-core owns the single omnibus cmd/evt bus; cross-boundary payloads are MessagePack bytes, not JSON. Never hold the host session lock while awaiting a library call: prepare PreparedTrackPlayback outside the lock. Any change to the bridge surface must stay in sync with the generated Dart API under apps/gui-flutter/lib/src/rust/. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

Shared traits and types (AudioBackend, AudioSource, StreamParams, DeviceId). These types are consumed by every other crate, so flag anything that widens a public signature, breaks a trait contract, or changes the dasp frame/sample representation. Keep this crate free of I/O and heavy dependencies. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

CPAL backend. Device capabilities must be read from CPAL at runtime (channel counts, sample-rate ranges) — flag hardcoded channel counts or sample rates. When opening a stream, prefer the 2-channel config with the lowest minimum sample rate and the smallest buffer size. The build callback is real-time: no allocation, no locking, no blocking. Low-latency/realtime features are the default backend behavior. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

SQLite persistence for Mixar's own library.db — schema, entity definitions, and migrations. Flag any unbounded query, missing index on a lookup column, transaction left open on an error path, or a schema change that is not paired with a migration. Waveforms, hot cues, and loops each live in their own dedicated table (track_waveform, track_hot_cue, track_loop) — keep new persisted data out of the tracks table. The sea-orm entity declaration (`#[sea_orm(table_name = "…", column_name = "…")]`) is authoritative: flag another hardcoded copy of the same table or column string in query code instead of reusing the entity or its column enum, and derive a migration version string from the chain instead of declaring it twice. Migrations are append-only: never rewrite a shipped migration — the frozen `library_schema_baseline` or an append-only rebuild such as `track_analysis_append_only` — to match renamed entities; a later schema change appends its own migration, and a test checks the whole chain against current entities. DDL is idempotent and must not drop, rename onto, or skip a same-named custom index; quote any identifier interpolated into PRAGMA or SQL; the declared column type must match what is written (RFC 3339 text is not an integer); automatic analysis and backfills must preserve the downbeat phase and downbeats array and must never overwrite a manual grid or BPM, or relabel a manual source; a user-authorized edit may replace the user's own manual data; keep backfills set-based; opening a database must go through the migrator and never run DDL itself, so two processes cannot both migrate; flag a nested `Db::transaction` call that can deadlock or be rejected as nested. Never block the caller while holding a database handle across an await. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

Versioned SQLite migration runner and its ledger. Every step runs in a transaction that rolls back and records no version when it fails; report a failure once, with its migration version and cause. Each step takes `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and rechecks the ledger after acquiring the write lock, so a version another opener already applied is not recorded twice — preserve those atomicity and at-most-once guarantees, and add a competing-opener regression test when that logic changes. The ledger's `applied_at` representation stays consistent within that ledger (integer epoch or RFC 3339 text), while `Status::applied_at` keeps normalizing to RFC 3339 text; flag only a mismatch between what `record` writes and what `status` reads back from the same ledger. Flag re-scanning the full ledger on every step (a query per version). Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

Shared library traits, types, and domain logic. This crate owns no database or backend access; its only file I/O is `LoadableAudio::load` for a library track (existence probe, decode), so flag any new I/O beyond that and keep decoding off the UI isolate. Flag anything that widens a public signature or breaks a trait contract consumed by library, library-db, or the adapters. Beat grid and tempo are canonical facts: preserve the downbeat phase and the downbeats array (never pin downbeat_offset_beats to 0), and define the manual-versus-analysis source so writers cannot overwrite a manual BPM or grid or relabel a manual source. Path, key, and metadata helpers must round-trip and reject malformed input rather than panicking. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

Library manager and external-library adapters (rekordbox, mixxx, CDJ). Mixar's own library.db goes through library-db entities — flag ad-hoc SQL, schema creation, or migrations against it outside library-db and migrator. External databases (a Mixxx collection, a rekordbox library) are opened read-only through their own connection and follow that format's contract; never write to them. Never hold the session or database lock across an await, and never block the caller while a database handle is open. Automatic analysis and imports must preserve the downbeat phase and downbeats array and must never overwrite manual hot cues, grids, or BPM, or relabel a manual source; a user-authorized edit may replace the user's own manual data. Adapters parse untrusted files: bounds-check lengths and counts, return errors instead of panicking or unwrapping, and confine paths only for operations defined to stay inside a root — a media reference read from a rekordbox or Mixxx database may point elsewhere, so validate it against the adapter's format and the user-selected scope. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

Decoding, resampling, and analysis. rubato is the resampler and symphonia the decoder. Flag fallible third-party calls that return an error that is then discarded with unwrap/expect, and any per-block allocation inside the sample-processing loop. Also cover analyzer output formats and thresholds when they change. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

Generated flutter_rust_bridge Dart surface. Verify it matches the bridge declared in crates/host-flutter, that no hand edit replaced generated output, and that every changed API has its callers under apps/gui-flutter/lib updated. A change here must come from `moon run gui-flutter:generate`. Do not review these files for widget style or hand-written lifecycle rules.

Flutter desktop UI. Dart bindings are generated by flutter_rust_bridge (`moon run gui-flutter:generate`), but the widgets are hand-written — apply Flutter review fundamentals directly: dispose every StreamSubscription, AnimationController, TextEditingController, ScrollController and any listener in dispose(); never call setState/context after dispose; never do async work in build(); use const constructors and avoid rebuild-all. Prefer Mixar shell widgets and `context.theme` tokens (Shad-bridged) over one-off chrome. Report errors concisely via showMixarToast, including async engine-start failures. Do not call raw host invoke/listen or the generated FRB API from widgets — go through EngineTransport, LibraryTransport and ControllerTransport with Riverpod, and never hand-edit the generated bridge. Performance controls (tempo, loops, hot cues) belong in bordered panels and must be disabled when no track is loaded. Never block the UI isolate with sync I/O or heavy decoding; hand work to a worker. Async and lifecycle: guard setState and context use after an await or dispose; where a finite animation's completion is awaited, use `.orCancel` and handle TickerCanceled — a repeating animation may run until it is disposed. Derive visible state from one source of truth — flag a tooltip or chip that disagrees with the enabled/audible state, an unawaited future that can leave a stale selection, two picks racing while one is in flight, an unbounded post-frame retry when the target's context is gone, and a dialog pushed on a nested navigator instead of the root one. Flag a Dart identifier that uses a reserved word (`new`, `class`, `default`) as a constructor or field name, a list wrapper that drops `super.key`, and a local that shadows a widget's field — rename the local instead. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

CI workflow review. Flag a `uses:` reference to a branch or tag that can move (e.g. @main, @v1) where a commit SHA would do, third-party actions that receive secrets while running untrusted PR code, missing `permissions:` blocks, `pull_request_target` combined with a checkout of the PR head, and PR-controlled values interpolated directly into a `run:` block instead of being passed through `env:`.

Rust review for `crates/`. Imports: flag a `use` block pulling items from two modules (`use foo::{Foo, bar::Bar}` — split it), a hand-rolled prelude module, and free functions imported so they can be called unqualified (call `module::function(…)`; importing types unqualified and importing a trait inside the function that uses it are both fine). Ownership: flag a newly added `Rc`/`Arc` with no stated reason — shared ownership is acceptable only for genuinely cross-thread or FRB state, never in the audio callback; flag a `.clone()` that exists to dodge borrowck, and any clone inside the audio callback or a per-block DSP loop; take `&T`/`&[T]`/`&str`/`Option<&T>` rather than `&Box<T>`/`&Vec<T>`/`&String`/`&Option<T>`. Traits and operators: flag inherent methods that duplicate a std trait (`from_str`, `to_string`, `from`, `default`) instead of the trait impl, and operator impls used as syntax sugar for non-mathematical work or an `Index` that can panic on ordinary input. Panics: flag `is_some()`/`is_ok()` checked and then `unwrap()`ed where `if let`/`match` proves the variant, `unwrap()` in non-test code (`expect` with the invariant instead), and assertions or `expect` messages that do not say why the invariant holds or which value broke it. Repo-wide: flag changed behavior that no test covers (existing coverage counts; a mechanical rename needs no test) and the removal of a test that pinned a format or contract; a local that shadows a field or outer binding; and a literal, fixture, wrapper, or decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper.

General review for this repo (Mixar, a Rust audio engine with a Flutter desktop UI). Security: flag hardcoded secrets or credentials, unvalidated paths or shell interpolation, and untrusted input reaching a database query or a process spawn. Correctness: flag duplicated logic that clearly belongs in an existing shared helper. Style: follow the surrounding code and the specs in docs/ — prefer minimal, focused changes over broad refactors. When a change touches a public API or a crate boundary, call out the cross-crate impact. Also check null/empty/zero/negative input; unchecked parsing and silent fallbacks; use-after-await of disposed context/ref/controllers and cancellation; locks held across await, check-then-act and stale snapshots; type/signature breaks across crates, the FRB boundary or callers; cache invalidation, wrong delegate/target and duplicate writes. Duplication: flag the same literal, SQL identifier, test setup wrapper, or theme decoration repeated in two or more places that must change together — extract one named constant or helper instead of copying it.
